title: Data Engineering
blurb: Model and move data reliably: warehouses and lakehouses, dbt and orchestration, Spark at scale, Kafka streaming, quality and governance.

quiz.question: Why are columnar formats fast for analytical queries?
options: Queries read only the needed columns, which compress well
quiz.explanation: Scanning one compressed column of a billion rows is far cheaper than reading whole rows.

quiz.question: What must you declare first when designing a fact table?
Which SCD type preserves history by adding a new row with validity dates?
quiz.explanation: Type 2 keeps each version with valid_from/valid_to so facts link to the version true at the time.

quiz.question: Re-running yesterday's load doubled the rows. What principle was violated?
quiz.explanation: Use MERGE or partition overwrite so reruns produce the same result.

quiz.question: One Spark task runs far longer than the others in a stage. Most likely cause?
options: Data skew on a hot key
quiz.explanation: Fix with AQE skew handling, separate null/hot keys, salting or broadcasting.

quiz.question: How is message ordering guaranteed in Kafka?
options: Within a partition, so key messages by the entity that needs ordering
quiz.explanation: All events with the same key go to the same partition and keep order.

quiz.question: What does a watermark do in stream processing?
options: Estimates event-time progress so windows can close and late events are bounded

quiz.question: What do open table formats such as Apache Iceberg add to files in object storage?
options: ACID transactions, schema evolution, time travel and efficient MERGE/deletes
quiz.explanation: They turn a data lake into a reliable lakehouse readable by many engines.

problems.title: Analytics model for a delivery app
problems.prompt: Design the warehouse model and pipeline for orders, deliveries and payments.
problems.solution: Bronze/silver/gold with CDC ingestion; facts at declared grains (order lines, deliveries, payments), conformed dimensions (date, customer SCD2, restaurant, rider, zone), dbt with unique/not_null/relationships/freshness tests and ledger reconciliation, Airflow DAG by data interval, idempotent MERGE loads, documented metrics.

problems.title: Real-time zone dashboard
problems.prompt: Show orders vs available riders per zone every 30 seconds.
problems.solution: CDC and rider events into Kafka keyed by zone, Flink tumbling event-time windows with a watermark, join with rider availability state, write to a low-latency store, schema registry compatibility, lag/freshness monitoring and alerts.
